payload.detail: LARGELY CLOSED, RE-MEASURED 2026-09-09 by Ward Lead. The row's central claim is now STALE. It said: 'THE REVERSAL IS NOT IN docs/ward-flow/owner-rulings-2026-09-04.md, so it exists only in one chat transcript.' It is now in that file, as R-2026-09-04-G, titled 'It suggests nothing is WITHDRAWN. The board is to match patients to beds.' The ruling records what the owner decided, the boundary that survives (the software never decides; final acceptance comes from the users), and the deliberate fact that it changes no behaviour yet — the prohibition is lifted and the matching work is to be planned as the next design, not started. AND THE FOUR SOURCE FILES ARE CORRECTED, verified individually rather than as a count: escalation-board.tsx and referral-destination-options.ts still contain the phrase but now carry its withdrawal immediately beside it ('It was never an owner ruling; it was inferred and then enforced. The owner has ruled the opposite'); ward-derivations.ts and escalation/page.tsx no longer contain it at all. So the P1 hazard this row was raised for — that the codebase actively instructs the next session to build the opposite, confidently — no longer holds. The ruling also states the distinction the correction had to make and which future comments must keep: DESCRIPTION 'this board does not rank wards' is true today and fine to write; INSTRUCTION 'this board MUST NEVER rank wards' is withdrawn and must not be written. WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION AND SHOULD NOT INHERIT THIS ROW'S FRAMING: the regulatory one. A board that ranks wards FOR A PATIENT is closer to clinical decision support than one that records what happened, the TGA/SaMD classification box was left unticked on PR #2597 for exactly that reason, and the ruling itself says lifting D4 is what turns it from hypothetical into live. Per the ruling it needs answering before this ships to anyone, not before it is prototyped — so it is a GATE, not a blocker on current work, and it belongs with the other pre-real-patient gates (R-2026-09-04-H sex/gender to a clinician, R-2026-09-04-I Aboriginal cultural safety review) rather than under a documentation-drift heading. Recommend this row be closed and the regulatory gate raised as its own item.
